items.title: Oil tankers burn as Iran's new leader vows to keep Strait of Hormuz closed
items.description: Iranian attacks on Gulf shipping, including two tankers set ablaze in Iraqi waters, have disrupted global oil supplies and sent prices soaring.

items.title: Trump says he is 'not happy' with Britain. Should Australia be nervous?
items.description: Many nations, including Australia, claim to have a special relationship with the United States. Britain, and some in Europe, are finding out that's no longer the case.

items.title: Fuel quality rules relaxed to rush 100 million litres into Australia's supply
items.description: Australia will bring in 100 million more litres of petrol by allowing a higher level of sulfur content in its fuel for the next 60 days, Energy Minister Chris Bowen says, as the country reckons with petrol flows choked by the Middle East war.

items.title: Motorists urged to stop panicking and hoarding fuel as oil price surges
items.description: The oil price has surged again amid Iranian strikes on oil tankers and the fear there could be more attacks to come.

items.title: Blues hang on for scratchy but vital win over Tigers at the MCG
items.description: Carlton kicks only one goal in the second half, but it is just enough to hold off a late charge by a wayward Richmond at the MCG.

items.title: Albanese government avoids the 'w' word
items.description: This week in Canberra the Nationals chose a new leader, the energy minister chose his words carefully and the government chose to avoid one word altogether.

items.title: 'Absolute madness': Broncos remain winless after Eels win bizarre NRL clash
items.description: The Broncos' defence is labelled "pathetic" as they surrender a 20-6 lead, hit back in the second half but eventually lose 40-32 on the back of future teammate Jonah Pezet's game-sealing try.

items.title: Grace Tame says her speaking events have stopped over 'smear campaign'
items.description: Former Australian of the Year Grace Tame says a conference in Hobart will be her last speaking engagement for the year, at this stage.

items.title: 'Black rain' in Tehran following Israeli strikes on oil depots
items.description: An Iranian man has told ABC News "black rain is falling from the sky" in Tehran in the wake of Israeli attacks on oil depots. The Iranian Red Crescent is warning residents to stay indoors and wear masks if possible due to the thick black smoke blanketing the capital. It's also urging residents to avoid contact with any further rain that may fall in the city, citing the risk of skin burns and lung damage from acidic rain.

items.title: Soldier accused of assaulting, robbing female colleague granted bail
items.description: A Darwin-based soldier accused of assaulting and robbing a fellow service person has been bailed to travel home to NSW.

items.title: Police accused of overreach after 'From the river to the sea' arrests
items.description: The pro-Palestinian group that organised the Brisbane protest says police were "everywhere" and "ready to make arrests" over use of the banned phrase.

items.title: Cruise ship had 'small margin for error' in poor light, report says
items.description: An early safety report into the grounding of luxury Australian cruise ship Coral Adventurer focuses on its speed and a wide turn in confined waters just before it swerved into a reef.

items.title: Parents shocked by sudden closure of specialist service for kids with autism
items.description: In a statement published on Wednesday, early intervention care provider AEIOU announced the board had appointed external administrators to the organisation.

items.title: Co-founder of Copenhagen's Noma steps down after abuse allegations
items.description: René Redzepi, co-founder of a restaurant repeatedly named the world's best, has announced he is stepping down after reports was abusive to staff at the famed Copenhagen restaurant.

items.title: We asked, you told: Dog ownership dos and don'ts
items.description: Here's how you can become a more responsible dog owner — according to your fellow readers.

items.title: Matildas stars Raso, Catley out of Asian Cup quarterfinal against North Korea
items.description: Hayley Raso and Steph Catley will miss the Women's Asian Cup quarterfinal, as the team prepares for the unknown quantities that North Korea may bring.

items.title: Another search, more frustration in Gus Lamont case
items.description: South Australian police have concluded their latest search for evidence following the disappearance of four-year-old Gus Lamont, but have not ruled out returning to the remote station where he lived.

items.title: Disaster payments have been expanded in the NT. Here's what you need to know
items.description: Residents in more flood-affected communities across the Top End are now eligible for hardship payments, with disaster assistance also extended further in the Barkly and central Australia.

items.title: 'Freight train' earthquake triggers precautionary checks at major dams
items.description: Two major regional NSW water storages will be inspected today following a magnitude-4.4 earthquake north of Canberra overnight.

items.title: Sophie Ellis-Bextor is embracing middle age on the dance floor
items.description: Megahits Murder on the Dancefloor and Groovejet made her a household name but Sophie Ellis-Bextor is so much more.

items.title: Quiz: Oscars winners and losers from the past 10 years
items.description: Test your knowledge of who went home with a statue and who was honoured just to be nominated.

items.title: The summers of today are vastly different to those of our grandparents
items.description: Australia has always been hot. On average, summer is now one degree warmer than it was 50 years ago. But that number hides the stark reality that the summers our kids experience today are much more extreme and longer than they used to be.

items.title: The rise of the 'manosphere' is being felt in the classroom
items.description: Teachers say misogynistic behaviour from young, male students has been getting worse. A guide has been released to help teachers, schools and young people recognise the manosphere's impacts and access tools to reclaim the classroom.

items.title: Coroner to examine whether 'unusual' death of Elizabeth Struhs was preventable
items.description: The Queensland coroner will examine interactions the Struhs family had with government agencies before the eight-year-old's death at the family's Toowoomba home in 2022.

items.title: Ex-ASIO boss says he's not needed, 'grossly overpaid' for royal commission
items.description: Former ASIO boss Dennis Richardson says he resigned from the royal commission into antisemitism because he felt he was overpaid and "surplus to requirements".
